Cursor AI prompt — Complete plan for a college-only social app (Flutter Android + Web + Node.js backend)

Use the full brief below to generate a complete, production-ready implementation plan and starter code for a college-only social media app (Instagram-like UX + Reddit-style topics + chats + stories). Produce code files, schemas, API routes, and ready-to-run sample projects for both backend and Flutter frontend. Be explicit, concrete, and opinionated — include everything a small dev team (or a single dev) needs to ship an MVP and iterate.

⸻

Project summary (single-sentence)

Build a cross-platform (Flutter Android + Web) social app limited to students of a single college that supports Google sign-in (restricted to college email), pre-created student accounts (immutable studentId), Instagram-style feed and stories, Reddit-style topics, chat, notifications, and Cloudinary media storage organized by year/department/section.

⸻

Goals & non-functional constraints
	•	Private scope: Only college email domain allowed for access (enforce server-side).
	•	Canonical id: studentId (college roll number) is the unique, immutable identifier for each user.
	•	Scalable & secure: Use HTTPS, verify Firebase ID tokens server-side, sign Cloudinary uploads server-side, use pagination and indexes for performance.
	•	Cross-platform: Single Flutter codebase for Android and Web (responsive UI).
	•	Modular: Clean separation: Auth (Firebase), Backend API (Node.js/Express + Mongoose), DB (MongoDB Atlas), Media (Cloudinary), Realtime (Socket.IO), Push (FCM).
	•	Deliverables must be runnable locally with sample data and clear README.

⸻

Target users & roles
	•	Students (primary): register via Google (college email), view feed, post, comment, DM, create topics, follow, join clubs later.
	•	Admins (secondary): upload roster CSV, moderate posts/topics, manage badges/clubs, view reports.

⸻

MVP feature list (must-have)
	1.	Firebase Google Sign-In restricted to college domain (server verifies domain).
	2.	Auto-created user records from preloaded roster (link to Google account at first sign-in).
	3.	Immutable studentId field on users.
	4.	Feed with posts (image/video/text), like, comment, basic pagination.
	5.	Stories (ephemeral for 24 hours).
	6.	Topics (reddit-style threads — create, comment, vote).
	7.	Direct Messages with real-time delivery (Socket.IO) and persisted history.
	8.	Notifications (in-app + FCM push).
	9.	Media uploads via Cloudinary with server-signed upload flow; folder scheme by year/dept/section/studentId.
	10.	Search & filters: by year, department, section, tags.
	11.	Admin web UI to upload roster CSV and moderate content.

⸻

Nice-to-have (later)
	•	Badges by year and role.
	•	Gamification and points system.
	•	Clubs and events.
	•	Advanced moderation / profanity filter / reporting dashboard.

⸻

Data models (exact JSON-style schemas — include types & indexes)

users
	•	Fields:
	•	_id: ObjectId
	•	studentId: string (immutable, unique) — e.g. "2025CS1001"
	•	email: string | null (college email when linked)
	•	displayName: string
	•	photoUrl: string | null
	•	year: number (1..4)
	•	department: string (CSE/ME/EC/…)
	•	section: string
	•	bio: string
	•	createdAt: Date
	•	joinedAt: Date | null
	•	badges: string[]
	•	fcmTokens: string[]
	•	settings: { notifications: boolean }
	•	Indexes:
	•	unique { studentId: 1 }
	•	{ email: 1 }
	•	compound { year:1, department:1, section:1 }

posts
	•	Fields:
	•	_id: ObjectId
	•	authorStudentId: string
	•	type: "image"|"video"|"text"
	•	media: [{ url:string, cloudinaryPublicId:string, width:number, height:number }] (optional)
	•	text: string
	•	visibility: "public" | "year" | "dept" | "section"
	•	tags: string[]
	•	likesCount: number
	•	commentsCount: number
	•	createdAt: Date
	•	Indexes:
	•	{ createdAt: -1 }, { authorStudentId: 1 }, text index on text

stories
	•	Fields:
	•	_id: ObjectId
	•	authorStudentId: string
	•	media: { url, cloudinaryId, duration }
	•	createdAt: Date
	•	expiresAt: Date (TTL index to auto-delete)
	•	TTL:
	•	Use Mongo TTL index on expiresAt.

topics
	•	Fields:
	•	_id: ObjectId
	•	title: string
	•	body: string
	•	authorStudentId: string
	•	votes: number
	•	tags: string[]
	•	commentsCount: number
	•	createdAt: Date

conversations / messages
	•	conversations:
	•	_id: ObjectId
	•	participants: [studentId...]
	•	lastMessage: string
	•	updatedAt: Date
	•	messages:
	•	_id
	•	conversationId
	•	senderStudentId
	•	text
	•	media (optional)
	•	createdAt
	•	readBy: [studentId...]
	•	Indexes:
	•	conversations compound { participants: 1, updatedAt: -1 }
	•	messages index { conversationId:1, createdAt:-1 }

notifications
	•	Fields:
	•	_id
	•	toStudentId
	•	type: "like"|"comment"|"follow"|"message"|"topic"
	•	meta: { postId?, fromStudentId?, topicId? }
	•	isRead: boolean
	•	createdAt: Date

⸻

API surface (Express-style endpoints with brief behavior rules)

Auth & account mapping
	•	POST /auth/firebaseSignIn
	•	Input: Firebase ID token from client
	•	Server: verify token with Firebase Admin SDK, ensure email endsWith @yourcollege.edu, find the users record by email OR ask client to provide studentId if roster lacks email mapping.
	•	Output: app JWT (or session), user doc.
	•	POST /auth/linkStudentId
	•	For manual mapping when roster has no email. Accept studentId and proof (OTP to college email). Enforce studentId uniqueness.

Users
	•	GET /users/:studentId
	•	PATCH /users/:studentId (only owner)
	•	GET /users?year=3&department=CSE&page=1

Posts
	•	GET /posts?cursor=...&filter=... (support visibility and filters)
	•	POST /posts (auth required — server verifies signed Cloudinary info before storing)
	•	POST /posts/:id/like
	•	POST /posts/:id/comment

Stories
	•	POST /stories (server returns Cloudinary signed params, client uploads)
	•	GET /stories?year=3

Topics
	•	GET /topics?tag=canteen
	•	POST /topics
	•	POST /topics/:id/vote
	•	POST /topics/:id/comment

Chat
	•	WebSocket (Socket.IO) real-time endpoint for messages, typing, read receipts.
	•	REST to fetch history: GET /conversations/:id/messages?limit=50

Notifications
	•	GET /notifications
	•	POST /notifications/markRead

Media
	•	POST /media/sign — returns signed Cloudinary params from server (server uses Cloudinary API secret)
	•	Optionally: POST /media/upload-proxy — server uploads for small files if desired

Admin
	•	POST /admin/roster — upload CSV to seed users
	•	GET /admin/reports
	•	POST /admin/moderate — remove/ban content or user

⸻

Cloudinary flow (precise)
	1.	Client requests POST /media/sign with file metadata (filename, mimeType, studentId, year, dept, section).
	2.	Server (Node/Express) uses Cloudinary SDK to create signed upload parameters and returns { signature, api_key, timestamp, folder }.
	3.	Client uploads directly to Cloudinary using returned params.
	4.	Cloudinary returns public_id and secure_url.
	5.	Client calls POST /posts with cloudinaryPublicId, secure_url, type, text, visibility, tags.
	6.	Server validates the public_id belongs to a permitted folder layout (guard against wrong folders).

Folder naming convention:
/collegeName/year-{year}/dept-{dept}/section-{section}/student-{studentId}/

Transformations: store original plus on-the-fly transformations for thumbnails.

⸻

Realtime & Push design
	•	Socket.IO for real-time chat, typing, presence, and instantly-delivered notifications when online.
	•	Redis adapter for Socket.IO when scaling to multiple instances.
	•	FCM for push: persist fcmTokens per users document; send pushes when recipient is offline.
	•	Delivery logic: on event, write notification doc -> emit via Socket.IO -> if not connected, send FCM.

⸻

Security & privacy rules (must be enforced)
	1.	Firebase ID token must be verified server-side on all protected endpoints.
	2.	Reject sign-in if email domain is not college domain. Log rejections.
	3.	studentId field is immutable in DB — enforce via schema and API permissions.
	4.	Cloudinary secrets never stored in client.
	5.	Rate limiting on activities (post creation, messaging) to prevent abuse.
	6.	Content moderation: reports collection and admin review flow.
	7.	Provide user opt-out and data deletion endpoints: DELETE /users/:studentId (admin + verification), GET /users/:studentId/export (data portability).

⸻

Flutter frontend requirements (deliverable)
	•	Project skeleton (single repo) with:
	•	lib/ folder organized: auth/, screens/, models/, services/, widgets/, providers/ (or riverpod setup).
	•	Implement Google sign-in using firebase_auth and google_sign_in.
	•	After sign-in, call POST /auth/firebaseSignIn to map to studentId and retrieve app JWT.
	•	Implement Home Feed screen: stories carousel, infinite-scroll feed (cursor-based), post composer (text + media), like/comment UI.
	•	Implement Post detail modal with comments.
	•	Implement Stories viewer (full-screen).
	•	Implement Topics list and topic detail with votes and comments.
	•	Implement Chat UI: conversation list, message thread, send images and text, show read receipts.
	•	Register for push notifications with firebase_messaging and post FCM token to backend.
	•	Profile screen: show immutable studentId, editable displayName/photo/bio.
	•	Search screen: filters for year/department/section and user list.
	•	Admin-only screens on web: roster upload page.
	•	Provide flutter pubspec.yaml with pinned versions and instructions to run for Android and Web.

⸻

Backend deliverables (deliverable)
	•	Node.js + Express project with:
	•	src/ structure: controllers/, routes/, models/ (Mongoose schemas), services/ (cloudinary, firebaseAdmin, fcm, socket), middleware/ (auth, rateLimit, errorHandler).
	•	Firebase Admin JWT verification middleware.
	•	Cloudinary sign route implementation.
	•	Example Mongoose schemas for users, posts, stories, topics, conversations, messages, notifications.
	•	Socket.IO server integrated, with Redis adapter commented as optional.
	•	Example tests / Postman collection or OpenAPI spec for endpoints.
	•	Dockerfile and docker-compose.yml to run backend + mongodb locally.
	•	README with setup steps, environment variables (Firebase service account, Cloudinary keys), and local dev instructions.

⸻

Admin UI deliverable
	•	Simple React or Next.js admin app (single file if needed) to:
	•	Upload roster CSV and seed users collection.
	•	Moderate posts/topics/reports.
	•	View basic metrics (daily active users, posts/day).
	•	Or provide API endpoints and README so user can build admin UI later.

⸻

Roadmap & milestones (priority order for Cursor to produce)
	1.	Generate backend Node.js project skeleton with Mongoose schemas + auth middleware + Cloudinary sign route + Socket.IO basic server.
	2.	Generate Flutter project skeleton implementing:
	•	Google sign-in + Firebase ID token exchange with backend
	•	Feed UI with dummy data and posts fetching
	•	Post composer flow that uses /media/sign then uploads to Cloudinary
	3.	Provide sample CSV roster and a script to seed DB.

	5.	Provide Postman collection or OpenAPI spec.

⸻

Acceptance criteria (how to verify MVP)
	•	When a user signs in with a college Google account, server maps them to a users document by email or asks for studentId input if necessary.
	•	The studentId for every user exists and cannot be changed by the user from the Flutter UI.
	•	Client can request Cloudinary signed params from /media/sign, upload directly to Cloudinary, and create a post referencing the returned public_id and URL.
	•	Feed returns paginated posts ordered by createdAt.
	•	Stories appear for 24 hours and are removed after TTL expiry.
	•	Real-time chat messages are transmitted via Socket.IO and persisted.
	•	Notifications are stored in DB and delivered via Socket.IO; if recipient is offline, FCM push is sent.
	•	Admin can upload roster CSV and seed database with user entries.

Implementation style & quality requirements
	•	Use modern, readable, idiomatic JavaScript (ES modules or CommonJS — pick one and be consistent).
	•	Provide clear code comments, and short usage examples above functions.
	•	For Flutter: use Provider or Riverpod for state management (pick one) and show a small example of a provider hooking up the auth state to the UI.
	•	Error handling and validation on all endpoints.
	•	Use environment variables for secrets — show .env.example.

⸻

Edge cases and decision rules (must be reflected)
	•	If roster CSV includes email field, auto-map on first sign-in. If not, require explicit studentId mapping with verification (OTP to college email) — provide API stub for OTP flow.
	•	If a user attempts sign-in with non-college email, return a clear error to client: "Access denied: school-domain required".
	•	Posts and topics may have visibility restricting who can view them; server must filter feed results accordingly.
	•	Enforce file size limits for uploads; if uploaded video exceeds allowed duration/size, reply with helpful error.
	•	All timestamps must be ISO 8601 UTC.

⸻

Priorities (what to implement first)
	1.	Firebase sign-in + server-side verification + studentId mapping.
	2.	Cloudinary signed upload flow + post creation.
	3.	Feed retrieval and pagination with indexes.
	4.	Stories with TTL.
	5.	Socket.IO chat + FCM fallback.
	6.	Admin roster upload.

Be explicit about any trade-offs (e.g., Socket.IO vs WebRTC for messages, storing media thumbnails vs on-the-fly transforms).
